timeline_highlights.title: Trump Issues Threats Against Iranian Infrastructure Amid Strait of Hormuz Tensions
timeline_highlights.summary: US President Donald Trump has threatened to target Iranian bridges and power plants in retaliation for any attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz. He stated that for each ship fired upon by Iranian forces, the US would respond by destroying a corresponding piece of Iranian infrastructure. This escalation comes amid ongoing tensions in the region and rising oil prices.
key_facts: Trump threatened to destroy Iranian infrastructure for each ship attacked in the Strait of Hormuz.
The threat follows continued Iranian attacks on shipping in the region.
Oil prices have surged amid the escalating tensions.

timeline_highlights.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky announced that Russian, Ukrainian, and US negotiators may meet soon to discuss ending the war. This statement follows a series of missile and drone strikes by Russia on Kyiv, which resumed after a brief pause for US peace talks, resulting in two fatalities and significant damage in the city.

timeline_highlights.title: Iran Launches Retaliatory Attacks Following US Strikes on Tankers
timeline_highlights.summary: In a significant escalation of hostilities, Iran launched ballistic missile attacks on a US military base in Jordan, responding to the US military's destruction of five Iranian oil tankers. The US strikes were a reaction to Iran's missile attempts against American warships in the Gulf of Oman. This exchange marks a deepening of the ongoing conflict between the two nations, which has seen increased violence over the past six months.
key_facts: Iran attacked a US base in Jordan with ballistic missiles.
The US destroyed five Iranian oil tankers in response to missile attacks on its warships.
The conflict has escalated over the past six months.

The US reportedly attacked five Iranian oil tankers, prompting Iran to retaliate by targeting ships near the Strait of Hormuz. This surge in oil prices has raised concerns about inflation and market stability worldwide.

event_overview.title: About Iran War
event_overview.subject: Iran War
event_overview.summary: “Iran War” is a shorthand for the 2026 armed conflict centered on direct U.S.-Iran hostilities, Iranian attacks and alleged attacks involving states around the Persian Gulf, and disruptions to maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. The United States calls its campaign Operation Epic Fury and says it began to protect U.S. forces, regional partners and navigation; Iran has described the U.S. and Israeli actions as unlawful aggression.

facts.label: Start of direct U.S. operation
facts.value: U.S. Central Command says Operation Epic Fury against Iran began on February 28, 2026, at the President’s direction. In a March 10 letter to the UN Security Council, the United States said it had commenced combat operations on February 28 in cooperation with Israel.

facts.label: Parties and regional reach
facts.value: The conflict directly involves the United States and Iran, with the United States describing Israel as an ally in its initial operations. UN Security Council resolution 2817 (2026) addressed attacks attributed to Iran against Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Jordan.

facts.label: Strategic waterway
facts.value: The Strait of Hormuz lies between Iran and Oman and connects the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman and Arabian Sea. It is a major oil and liquefied-natural-gas transit chokepoint, so threats to shipping there can have wider energy-market effects.

facts.label: Competing legal positions
facts.value: The United States notified the Security Council that it was acting in self-defense under Article 51 of the UN Charter. Iran has told the Council that the U.S. and Israeli campaign constituted aggression and that subsequent Iranian measures were self-defense; these are opposing state positions, not a judicial determination.

facts.label: U.S. constitutional and statutory contex
facts.value: Under the War Powers Resolution, U.S. policy is that the collective judgment of Congress and the President should apply to the introduction and continued use of U.S. armed forces in hostilities; the statute identifies a declaration of war, specific statutory authorization, or a national emergency created by attack as bases for introducing forces into hostilities.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers a limited set of developments from July 22-27, 2026—military threats, congressional war-powers action, shipping and oil-market pressure, Houthi claims, and ceasefire diplomacy—not the conflict’s full origins, all operations, or its eventual outcome.

related_stories.title: Tehran Launches Missile Strikes on U.S. Base in Jordan Following Tanker Destruction
related_stories.summary: Tehran has retaliated against the U.S. by launching a barrage of 20 ballistic missiles at a U.S. military base in Jordan. This action follows the U.S. destruction of five Iranian oil tankers, which was preceded by missile attacks from the Iranian Revolutionary Guard Corps on a U.S. Navy warship. The situation escalated as Tehran also issued warnings to tankers near Kuwait and Bahrain to evacuate.
